mutant:features/duplicates.feature#A fol.reason: All eight are invariance by design, which is the scenario purpose. Do not prune these rows as duplicative. REVISIT TRIGGER: void if SUPPLEMENTAL and REOPENED ever resolve differently from one another, or if any notice type exclusion becomes conditional on timing.

mutant:features/duplicates.feature#Match.reason: Three distinct mechanisms, recorded under one reason only because approval is scoped per scenario and not per mutant - read this as three records. (a) Rows excluded by policy (AU-7654321) or by loss type (water_damage): the row already yields no match on a dimension the mutation does not touch, so no value in the mutated column can change the outcome. (b) Rows excluded by loss-date distance (2026-08-01, 2026-04-01): these agree with the existing claim on both policy and loss type; what excludes them is the date sitting one day outside the window, so mutating either agreeing column is inert. (c) Matching rows whose loss_date is swapped for another matching row value (2026-06-01, 2026-07-31, 2026-04-02): the substituted date is also within 60 days, so the match survives - a swap to 2026-08-01 or 2026-04-01 flips the result and is killed, meaning the plus/minus 60 boundary is proven by those pairs jointly and never by a single row. REVISIT TRIGGER: (b) and (c) are void if the window changes from 60 days; (a) is void if policy or loss-type equality stops being part of the match key.

mutant:features/siu_indicators.feature#A.reason: Guard-dominated. The mutated value is the UPPER bound, but this scenario exercises the LOWER bound: the inception date postdates the loss date, so the `0 <=` check in _is_recent_inception rejects the negative interval before the upper bound is consulted. The upper bound is unreachable here at any value. REVISIT TRIGGER: void if the `0 <=` lower bound is removed, relaxed, or replaced.

mutant:features/siu_indicators.feature#B.reason: Margin, not inertness. The threshold is doing its job; the example values sit far enough from it that a plus-or-minus-one mutation cannot cross the boundary - 62 days against 45/46, and 40 days against both 45/46 and 30/31. The boundaries themselves are proven in the dedicated boundary scenarios, which are where a one-day mutation does kill. REVISIT TRIGGER: void if either scenario's example dates are changed such that an interval lands within one day of its threshold.

mutant:features/triage.feature#From raw.reason:
Ten of these eleven survivors are ordinary equivalents: the mutated value produces identical severity, queue, and both SIU flags. Loss amount is irrelevant to severity for fire and water_damage (severity derives from loss type) and remains under the $500 threshold for theft; the $500 boundary is separately proven in the "Theft severity by loss amount" rule. Inception mutations to 2026-05-15 against a 2026-08-01 loss date are 78 days out, outside the 30-day window either way.

The eleventh survivor — the row where the mutated inception date postdates the loss date (theft / 2026-06-15), inception_date 2024-01-01->2026-07-20 — is different and this paragraph is its own record, not an extension of the above: unkillable at this layer, but NOT because the specification maps both values to the same outcome — the specification is silent. The mutated inception date (2026-07-20) postdates this row's loss date (2026-06-15), producing a negative interval that returns false only because of the `0 <=` lower bound in _is_recent_inception. That guard is undocumented: no scenario in siu_indicators.feature, triage.feature, or any unit test exercises an inception date later than a loss date. Structurally unavoidable rather than a data-choice artifact: this scenario must exercise recent_inception=true (requiring an inception within 30 days of that row's loss date) and late_reporting=true (requiring a loss date more than 30 days before today). Together those guarantee some inception value in the column postdates some loss date in the column. No arrangement of the example data avoids it while still covering both indicators. REVISIT TRIGGER, applying only to the mutant on the row where the mutated inception date postdates the loss date (theft / 2026-06-15), not the other ten: this approval is void if the `0 <=` lower bound in _is_recent_inception is removed, relaxed, or replaced. It is the only thing making this mutant survive, and nothing else in the suite would catch its removal.

When that lands, re-run these mutants rather than carrying the approval forward.
